result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: Section 431.30(b) lists two things an answer must contain.
claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
(2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.

claims.claim: The answer must contain a general or specific denial of the material allegations the defendant disputes.
claims.quote: (1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.

claims.claim: The answer must state any new matter that constitutes a defense.
claims.quote: (2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.

claims.claim: Whether a general denial is sufficient depends on the complaint; it is sufficient if the complaint is not verified.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient
claims.note: This is the statutory rule about the denial, not permission to use PLD-050 in every such case.

claims.claim: A general denial is also sufficient for a complaint subject to Article 2, commencing with Section 90 of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1, subject to the draft’s verified assigned-claim exception.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient
claims.note: The draft separately states the exception.

claims.claim: A general denial puts only the complaint’s material allegations in issue.
claims.quote: a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.

claims.claim: For a verified complaint not subject to Article 2, the denial must be made positively or according to the defendant’s information and belief.
claims.quote: If the complaint is verified, unless the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1, the denial of the allegations shall be made positively or according to the information and belief of the defendant.

claims.claim: For a verified complaint on a claim assigned to a third party for collection, the same denial requirement applies even under Article 2.
claims.quote: However, if the cause of action is a claim assigned to a third party for collection and the complaint is verified, the denial of the allegations shall be made positively or according to the information and belief of the defendant, even if the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1.
claims.note: This statutory exception has no dollar threshold.

claims.claim: Each defense must be stated separately.
claims.quote: The defenses shall be separately stated

claims.claim: The defenses must identify the causes of action they answer so the defenses can be distinguished.
claims.quote: the several defenses shall refer to the causes of action which they are intended to answer, in a manner by which they may be intelligibly distinguished.

claims.claim: Limited civil classification under Section 85 requires all its conditions to be met.
claims.quote: an action or special proceeding shall be treated as a limited civil case only if all of the following conditions are satisfied:

claims.claim: One Section 85 condition is an amount in controversy of $35,000 or less.
claims.quote: (a) The amount in controversy does not exceed thirty-five thousand dollars ($35,000).
claims.note: The draft does not treat this condition alone as sufficient.

claims.claim: SUM-100 gives the defendant 30 calendar days after service to file a written response at the court.
claims.quote: You have 30 CALENDAR DAYS after this summons and legal papers are served on you to file a written response at this court
claims.note: Service here refers to service of the summons and legal papers on the defendant.

claims.claim: SUM-100 says to have a copy served on the plaintiff within that period.
claims.quote:
You have 30 CALENDAR DAYS after this summons and legal papers are served on you to file a written response at this court and have a copy
served on the plaintiff.

claims.claim: SUM-100 says a defendant who cannot pay the filing fee can ask the court clerk for a fee waiver form.
claims.quote:
If you cannot pay the filing fee, ask the
court clerk for a fee waiver form.

claims.claim: PLD-050 is General Denial, revised January 1, 2024.
claims.quote: Judicial Council form PLD-050 (General Denial), Rev. January 1, 2024

claims.claim: A defendant filing a general denial must use PLD-050 if the amount asked for or the value of the property involved is $1,000 or less.
claims.quote:
If you want to file a general denial, you MUST use this form if the amount asked for in the complaint or the value of the property
involved is $1,000 or less.
claims.note: The form choice is mandatory only when filing a general denial.

claims.claim: PLD-050 permits use for an unverified complaint, subject to the stated assigned-claim exclusion.
claims.quote:
You MAY use this form for a general denial if
1. The complaint is not verified; or

claims.claim: PLD-050 permits use for a verified complaint in a limited civil case, subject to the stated exclusion, and describes the amount in controversy as $35,000 or less.
claims.quote:
You MAY use this form for a general denial if
1. The complaint is not verified; or
2. The complaint is verified and the case is a limited civil case (the amount in controversy is $35,000 or less),
BUT NOT if the complaint involves a claim for more than $1,000 that has been assigned to a third party for collection.

claims.claim: PLD-050 excludes a complaint involving a claim for more than $1,000 assigned to a third party for collection.
claims.quote: BUT NOT if the complaint involves a claim for more than $1,000 that has been assigned to a third party for collection.
claims.note: The draft does not limit this form restriction to verified complaints.

claims.claim: The original general denial must be filed with the court clerk.
claims.quote: The original of this General Denial must be filed with the clerk of this court

claims.claim: Filing requires proof that a copy was served on each plaintiff’s attorney and each unrepresented plaintiff.
claims.quote:
with proof that a copy was served on each plaintiff's
attorney and on each plaintiff not represented by an attorney.

claims.claim: FW-001 is Request to Waive Court Fees, revised April 1, 2024.
claims.quote: Judicial Council form FW-001 (Request to Waive Court Fees), Rev. April 1, 2024

claims.claim: Receiving public benefits is one stated ground for using FW-001 to request a waiver.
claims.quote:
If you are getting public benefits, are a low-income person, or do not have
enough income to pay for your household’s basic needs and your court fees, you
may use this form to ask the court to waive your court fees.

claims.claim: Being a low-income person is another stated ground for using FW-001 to request a waiver.
claims.quote:
If you are getting public benefits, are a low-income person, or do not have
enough income to pay for your household’s basic needs and your court fees, you
may use this form to ask the court to waive your court fees.

claims.claim: Insufficient income to pay both household basic needs and court fees is another stated ground for using FW-001 to request a waiver.
claims.quote:
or do not have
enough income to pay for your household’s basic needs and your court fees, you
may use this form to ask the court to waive your court fees.

result.summary: The supplied texts support the claims within the stated scope. The draft distinguishes when a general denial is sufficient under §431.30(d) from when PLD-050 may be used: the form’s $1,000 exclusion does not set a dollar threshold for the statute’s verified assigned-claim rule.
